thread:
morgan: Heads-up — customer hit double billing when a streaming request got routed mid-stream to a cheaper fallback. Console showed a provisional token row then a committed row but numbers didn't add up. Can we clarify ownership semantics?

ada: Ugh. Do we have a trace of the routing decision + the stream_chunks? I want to see whether the fallback started a new billing span or reused the original.

morgan: Pasted the relevant trace snippet below (redacted ids). Looks like router forwarded to model-b-quant at chunk 42, we emitted a `provisional_charge` metric and then later a `final_charge` for the same session but both were counted.

morgan: ```
TRACE ID: tr-9a7
route: model-a -> model-b-quant (fallback) @ chunk=42
metrics: provisional_tokens=483 final_tokens=510
billing_events: provisional_emitted=true final_emitted=true
logs: router: "handoff created billing_anchor=anc-123"
```

kai: So the problem is we treat provisional as reserved and then also commit without de-duplicating on the anchor. We probably need a single canonical "billing anchor" that all downstream paths check before emitting a final charge.

ada: Do we rely on client idempotency keys today? That seems brittle for reconnects — many customers reconnect with new session ids. We should probably make the server-side anchor authoritative.

morgan: Proposal: internal API adds an optional header `x-rw-billing-anchor` that router sets on first accept. Downstream model servers echo it back in stream delta events as `billing_anchor`. Billing service will dedupe on anchor+sequence-range. Example:

morgan: ```http
POST /v1/generate
Host: internal-rw
X-RW-Billing-Anchor: anc-123
Content-Type: application/json
{ "prompt": "..." }
```

morgan: And stream events include 
```json
{ "event": "delta", "text": "...", "billing_anchor": "anc-123", "chunk_index": 42 }
```

ada: That sounds reasonable. Two questions: 1) what happens if we swap model and the downstream doesn't understand the header? 2) how do we show this in Console so support can explain provisional vs committed?

kai: For (1) we should have router attach the anchor as metadata in the in-memory handoff and, if a model doesn't echo it, the handoff still records it and billing service can stitch based on trace id + anchor. But best to require the internal contract — we'll add a compatibility flag to node agents during rollout.

sanjay: On quotas: are provisional tokens counted against quota immediately? If so, customers might hit quota and block while we later decide to not commit (e.g., client cancels). We need separate metrics: `reserved_tokens` vs `consumed_tokens`.

morgan: Exactly. Proposal: Console -> per-route breakdown: Reserved (speculative) | Committed. Reserved reduces available quota until finalization or TTL expires. UI should show TTL and allow ops to clear stale reservations.

claire: I can do the Console mock. Suggestion: show a timeline bar under each request in the Debug view: gray = reserved, green = committed, red = reversed. Quick toggle to hide speculative charges in billing exports.

ada: Metrics we should add (PromQL examples):
morgan: ```promql
sum by(route) (rw_billing_reserved_tokens_total{env="prod"})
sum by(route) (rw_billing_committed_tokens_total{env="prod"})
```

ada: Also add a trace attribute `billing.anchor` so Sentry/OTel can link events.

kai: Rollout plan: modify router to emit anchor on accept (canary 10% traffic), update model nodes to echo header (gradual), add dedupe in billing service (feature flag off by default), enable Console UI in staging. If dedupe works then flip feature flag and expand canary.

ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: router-anchor-canary -> 2026-03-24T03:00Z, model-echo-agent -> 2026-03-25T04:00Z, billing-dedupe -> 2026-03-26T05:00Z. :white_check_mark:

sanjay: Edge-case: what about mid-stream tool calls? If the model issues a tool call that triggers external compute and returns text, we need to ensure the tool call tokens are attributed to the original anchor, not the tool container. Otherwise tool containers' meterings will be separate.

morgan: Good catch. We should propagate billing_anchor in toolcall RPCs as well. Add `billing_anchor` to toolcall context. Tools should not create new anchors.

claire: I'll own the Console PR (mock + small UX copy explaining "speculative" vs "committed"). Will link to docs for how quota reservations behave.

ada: I'll update internal API spec and add a compatibility table for older model backends.

kai: I'll implement dedupe in billing service and add end-to-end tests that simulate reconnects and midstream swaps. Tests should assert no double-charge within 24h if anchor matches.

morgan: Action items summary:
- router: attach anchor on accept (kai)
- model nodes: echo billing_anchor (ada)
- billing: dedupe on anchor+range (kai)
- console: show reserved vs committed + TTL controls (claire)
- docs: update internal API spec (ada)
- tests: end-to-end reconnect/handoff scenarios (kai + ada)

morgan: TL;DR: server-side billing anchor + reserved vs committed telemetry + Console UX should fix these double-bill cases and make support/debugging straightforward.

ada: SGTM. let's run canary and monitor `rw_billing_reserved_tokens_total` vs `rw_billing_committed_tokens_total` spikes. :rocket:

claire: I'll post the mock link in #eng-platform when ready.

morgan: thanks all. I'll create the epic and link PRs to it.
